topics.name: Prepositions of time (on, in, for, since)

questions.rule: Yesterday is in the past, so use the simple past: rained.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct preposition.
questions.rule: We use on with days: on Saturday, on Monday.
In a question, the helping verb comes before the subject: Where are you going?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Yesterday tells us it is past, so reach becomes reached.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: were + -ing makes the past continuous, like snoring: were sleeping.
We use in with months: in June, in August.
Last night is past. The simple past of blow is blew.
Subject (The road) + verb (was) + the rest: full of water.

chat: Did you go to school yesterday?
options: No, I didn't go. It rained a lot.
No, I didn't went. It rained a lot.
No, I not go. It rained a lot.
questions.rule: After didn't, use the base verb: didn't go, never didn't went.

chat: When is Dahi Handi this year?
questions.rule: We use on with dates: on 27 August.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: People was waiting at the bus stop when the rain began.
People were wait at the bus stop when the rain began.
People were waiting at the bus stop when the rain began.
questions.rule: People is plural, so use were + verb-ing: were waiting.

options: Many roads was submerged last night.
Many roads were submerged last night.
Many roads are submerged last night.
questions.rule: Last night is past and roads is plural, so use were.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: For a length of time, use for: for three days.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After did, use the base verb: did ... become.
A longer past action (were having) was interrupted by a short one (went out).

questions.after: people were injured in the accident?
questions.rule: People can be counted, so ask How many.
A yes/no question starts with the verb: Are you ready...?
Who did it + past verb + what: The officials closed the road.

chat: What were you doing when the lights went out?
questions.rule: The question is in the past continuous, so answer I was reading.

chat: Rohan, ask me one question about the flood.
options: How many houses did the water damage?
How many houses the water damaged?
How many houses did the water damaged?
questions.rule: Past question: did + subject + base verb: did the water damage?

options: The children were playing outside when it start to rain.
The children were playing outside when it started to rain.
The children was playing outside when it started to rain.
questions.rule: Long action: were playing. Short action that broke in: started.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct preposition.
options: It has been raining since Monday.
It has been raining for Monday.
It has been raining at Monday.
questions.rule: Use since with a starting point: since Monday. Use for with a length of time.
With you, use Do, and the verb stays in base form: Do you need?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: were + -ing makes the past continuous, like carrying: were building.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Five hours is a length of time, so use for.
Last week is past, so use the simple past: entered.

questions.after: you see the landslide on the news last night?
questions.rule: Last night is past, so the question starts with Did.
Long action first (was raining), then when + short action (we left).

chat: Did the trains run on time today?
options: No, they runned very late because of the rain.
No, they didn't ran on time because of the rain.
No, they ran very late because of the rain.
questions.rule: Run is irregular: past is ran. After didn't, use run.

chat: How long did you wait for the bus?
questions.rule: An hour is a length of time, so use for.

options: An officials said that five people lost their lives.
An official said that five peoples lost their lives.
An official said that five people lost their lives.
questions.rule: An goes with one thing: an official. People is already plural.

options: The traffic was moving very slowly on the bridge.
The traffic were moving very slowly on the bridge.
The traffic was move very slowly on the bridge.
questions.rule: Traffic is uncountable and takes was; past continuous = was moving.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Injured begins with a vowel sound, so use an: an injured man.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Water cannot be counted, so use much, not many.

questions.after: watching the news when the phone rang.
questions.rule: My brother and I = two people (we), so use were.

questions.after: absent because of the flood yesterday?
questions.rule: Students is plural and yesterday is past, so use were.
Result first (shops stayed closed), then the reason: because of the flood.
Wh- word + did + subject + base verb: Why did the school close early?

chat: What did you carry in your bag during the storm?
options: I carried a umbrella and a torch.
I carried an umbrella and a torch.
I carried an umbrella and an torch.
questions.rule: an before a vowel sound (an umbrella), a before a consonant sound (a torch).

options: No, they wasn't. Many roads were under water.
No, they weren't. Many road were under water.
No, they weren't. Many roads were under water.
questions.rule: They takes weren't; after many, the noun is plural: many roads.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: While people were celebrating Dahi Handi, heavy rain lash the city.
While people were celebrating Dahi Handi, heavy rain lashed the city.
While people was celebrating Dahi Handi, heavy rain lashed the city.
questions.rule: While + past continuous (were celebrating), then simple past (lashed).

options: Do you know when did the rescue team reach the spot?
Do you know when the rescue team reach the spot?
Do you know when the rescue team reached the spot?
questions.rule: Inside Do you know ...?, keep normal order and no did: when the team reached.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: 27 August is a date, so use on: on 27 August.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The whole sentence is in the past, so waits must be waited.

questions.before: Schools in the city stayed closed
questions.after: two days after the heavy rain.
questions.rule: Two days is a length of time, so use for.

questions.before: Can you tell me where the relief camp
questions.rule: After Can you tell me where, use normal order: the relief camp is.
Past continuous question: Were + subject + verb-ing: Were the children sleeping...?
How long + did + subject + base verb: did the heavy rain last?

chat: What did the officials do after the landslide?
options: They shifted the injured to hospitals and close the road.
They shifted the injured to hospitals and closed the road.
They shift the injured to hospitals and closed the road yesterday.
questions.rule: Both actions are past, so both verbs take the past: shifted ... closed.

chat: Where were you when the landslide happened?
options: I was at my uncle's house, and we was watching the news.
I was at my uncle's house, and we were watching the news.
I were at my uncle's house, and we were watching the news.
questions.rule: I was, we were: match was/were to the subject.
